item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Each figure represents a fraction.

[Image: Four figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4]

Which two figures represent the same fraction?
item.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4:
- Figure 1: A rectangle divided vertically into 4 equal strips; the 3 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 2: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 4 columns (8 equal parts); the 2 parts in the first column on the left are unshaded white, and the 6 parts in the other 3 columns are shaded gray.
- Figure 3: A rectangle divided vertically into 3 equal strips; the 2 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 4: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 2 columns (4 equal parts); the 2 parts in the left column are unshaded white, and the 2 parts in the right column are shaded gray.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Figures that are the same size and shape are called congruent figures.

[Image: Four figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4]

Which two figures are congruent?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectilinear figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4:
- Figure 1: An L-shaped polygon with a horizontal top arm extending to the right and a vertical arm on the left extending downwards.
- Figure 2: A large rectangular/square shape with a small rectangular tab extending out to the upper right.
- Figure 3: An L-shaped polygon with a tall vertical left arm and a shorter horizontal bottom arm extending to the right.
- Figure 4: An L-shaped polygon with a horizontal bottom arm extending to the left and a vertical arm on the right extending upwards, having the same arm lengths and thickness as Figure 1 rotated 180 degrees.

reference_items.stem:

Figures 1, 2, and 3 are shown below.

He needs four matches to form figure 1, seven matches to form figure 2, and ten matches to form figure 3.

He uses the same rule each time to make the next figure in the pattern.

reference_items.stem:

Which diagram has 3 out of every 4 squares shaded?
reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes a diagram of a rectangle divided into 2 rows of 3 equal squares (6 squares total). The 4 squares in the first two columns are shaded grey, and the 2 squares in the third column are unshaded (white).

The response options show four diagrams composed of squares:
- Option A: A horizontal row of 3 equal squares, all 3 shaded grey.
- Option B: A horizontal row of 4 equal squares; the first 3 squares are unshaded and the 4th square is shaded grey.
- Option C: A vertical rectangle divided into 4 rows of 2 equal squares (8 squares total). The top 6 squares (3 rows) are shaded grey, and the bottom 2 squares (1 row) are unshaded.
- Option D: A horizontal row of 6 equal squares; the first 3 squares are shaded grey and the last 3 squares are unshaded.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Ahmed made a survey of the favorite color of the students in 4 classes.

[Image: Four bar graph figures labeled Class 1, Class 2, Class 3, Class 4 with 3 columns labeled Red, Green, and Blue on x-axis. Y-axis with values of 0 to 14 for Class 1 and Class 4 and values of 0 to 15 for Class 2 and Class 3.
• Class 1: Red value of 12, Green value of 10, Blue value of 8.
• Class 2: Red value of 10, Green value of 15, Blue value of 5.
• Class 3: Red value of 5, Green value of 10, Blue value of 15.
• Class 4: Red value of 7, Green value of 10, Blue value of 13.]

In which class do the fewest students choose blue?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four bar graphs arranged in a 2-by-2 grid, each showing student choices for favorite colors (Red, Green, Blue):
- Class 1 (top-left): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 14 in increments of 2, with grid lines at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is shaded gray with a height of 12; Green is shaded black with a height of 10; Blue is unshaded (white) with a height of 8.
- Class 2 (top-right): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 15 in increments of 5, with grid lines at 0, 5, 10, and 15. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 10; Green is black with a height of 15; Blue is white with a height of 5.
- Class 3 (bottom-left): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 15 in increments of 5, with grid lines at 0, 5, 10, and 15. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 5; Green is black with a height of 10; Blue is white with a height of 15.
- Class 4 (bottom-right): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 14 in increments of 2, with grid lines at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 7; Green is black with a height of 10; Blue is white with a height of 13.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
